claims.text: A graded Ni-based interlayer improves the adhesion of an HEA coating to a Cu substrate.
A graded Ni-based interlayer improves the durability of a Cu/HEA composite under wear and thermal cycling.
The Cu substrate may retain a native oxide layer after polishing.
A refractory HEA coating can serve as a wear-resistant surface layer.
HEA coatings can be deposited on lower-cost substrates as an alternative to bulk HEAs.
The Ni-based interlayer mediates interdiffusion bonding at the Cu/HEA interface.
A gradual compositional transition from Cu to the HEA reduces thermal-expansion mismatch.
Interfacial diffusion promoted by the graded Ni-based interlayer produces metallurgical bonding.
The graded interlayer reduces stress concentrations caused by thermal-expansion differences.
Reduced interfacial stress and improved metallurgical bonding increase resistance to delamination during wear and thermal cycling.
The Ni-interlayer system will have higher adhesion strength than direct HEA deposition on Cu.
The Ni-interlayer system will have a lower wear rate than direct HEA deposition on Cu.
The Ni-interlayer system will have greater interfacial stability during thermal cycling than direct HEA deposition on Cu.
Direct deposition of an HEA coating on Cu has inferior adhesion because of poor metallurgical bonding.
Direct deposition of an HEA coating on Cu has inferior adhesion because of mismatched thermal properties.
The proposed benefit is limited to conditions in which interfacial bonding is the primary failure challenge.
Extreme thermal mismatch or environmental corrosion may dominate failure and limit the interlayer's benefit.
